newsitem.title: INDIA: One dead, 34 said trapped in India house collapse.
newsitem.headline: One dead, 34 said trapped in India house collapse.

text.p: One person died and at least 34 were feared trapped when a four-storey building collapsed in the heart of India's commercial capital of Bombay on Tuesday, fire brigade officials said.
"We fear there are 34 people trapped," Chief Fire Officer D.J. Kulkarni of the Bombay Fire Brigade told Reuters. "We have removed nine injured people. There was also one dead body."
The building, divided into residential flats and offices, collapsed shortly after noon. It was not immediately known why it came down.
"It collapsed like a pack of cards," said T.L. D'Souza, who works in a garage nearby. "Suddenly it fell. Within five minutes it was down -- flattened. No noise, no shouts for help."

Civic officials estimate that more than 20,000 buildings in the city are in danger of imminent collapse because of poor maintenance. But many residents have refused to move out because they have nowhere else to go to.

The building housed a printing press on the ground floor with apartments, courier agencies, tailoring shops, and a lawyer's office on the upper floors. It was located at the centre of a dense cluster of similar buildings.
